profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap way, tagged telecom=data_center and named "Newrays Two LLC Mining," is located in Tennessee and is self-identified by name as a mining operation run under the entity Newrays Two LLC. The word "Mining" in an operator's own facility name, combined with a telecom=data_center tag, is a pattern seen repeatedly among cryptocurrency mining hosting sites that have been tagged in OpenStreetMap using the same general-purpose data-center key used for traditional colocation and cloud facilities, even though the underlying use case is materially different: racks of application-specific mining hardware drawing power for proof-of-work computation rather than general enterprise servers or cloud infrastructure serving external customers over a network uplink. Tennessee has attracted a number of such operations in recent years, often near favorable power pricing or surplus generation capacity. A Tennessee Secretary of State corporate registration for an entity named Newrays Two LLC would be the natural next primary source to confirm formation date and registered agent, and operator or trade-press coverage would help confirm hardware scale and site history, but neither could be retrieved this session due to search-tool quota limits. This entry should be read as a cryptocurrency mining hosting facility rather than a general-purpose data center, pending that fuller confirmation.

reading.body:
This facility record exists in the registry as a mapped location in Henry County, Tennessee, but cannot be resolved to an operator, a website, or published specifications. The name "Newrays Two LLC Mining" appears in no discoverable source beyond the mapping data itself. Reverse geocoding the stored coordinates returns only a street address with no business identifier. Without a website or operator contact information on file, no technical specifications are available to assess the campus's power capacity, cooling capability, or AI hosting fitness.

Tennessee has published specifications from only four of its twenty-four mapped data center facilities, totaling 12.13 MW of disclosed capacity. This facility ranks fifth by published megawatts in the state, which means it either publishes no capacity figure or the published figure places it below the four disclosed sites. The state's mapped footprint is sparse relative to major AI infrastructure regions, and this facility's unresolved operator status means it contributes no verified data to any assessment of Tennessee's role in AI scaling.

Without operator identity, published power, or technical certifications, this facility cannot be evaluated for its capacity to host AI workloads. Future research with working search tools or manual verification may resolve the operator and unlock the specifications needed to read what this location means for the grid.
